chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Ḥammād ibn Ziyād, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

ʿAlī عليه السلام was asked about a mukātab who falsely accused a Muslim man, so he said: “He is to be given the hadd of a free man, eighty lashes, whether he has paid anything of his mukātabah or has not paid.”

It was said to him: “What if he commits zina while he is a mukātab and has not paid anything of his mukātabah?” He said: “This is the right of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Fifty lashes are removed from him, and he is given fifty.”

key_terms.جَلْدَةً: A single lash in corporal punishment.
key_terms.حَقُّ ٱللَّهِ: A right belonging to Allah, referring to a divinely prescribed legal claim.
key_terms.مُكَاتَبٍ: A slave under a contractual agreement to earn or purchase freedom.
key_terms.ٱفْتَرَى: Falsely accused or fabricated a charge against someone.
key_terms.ٱلْحُرِّ: A free person, whose legal punishment is the standard being referenced.

ai.seo_question: What is the legal punishment for a mukātab who commits slander or zina in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the hadd punishments of a mukātab. In the case of slanderous accusation, he receives the punishment of a free man, while in zina, because it is a right of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, the punishment is reduced to fifty lashes when he has not paid anything of his contract.
